answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk, with transition mass weighted by verified edges, so influence cannot leap across unsupported identities. A Sybil cluster usually attaches to honest nodes through a sparse external cut; its low conductance bounds the probability of escape, while min-cut transitivity bounds the aggregate voting weight it can accumulate, regardless of internal Sybil count. Nodes labeled tide, lantern, and opal gain weight only through accountable bridges.
